label: DIR-3 KYC not filed by 30 September for a director
best_case: You file a day late, pay the ₹5,000 reactivation fee, and move on.
worst_case: The DIN deactivates on 1 October. You can't sign any MCA filing, including the ones needed to fix other problems, until it's reactivated and the fee paid, and it happens the same week a customer wants a signed board resolution.

sources.title: DIR-3 KYC 2026: due date, fees and common errors

note: Probability estimated as a once-a-year deadline event; weekly figure spread across the year with a spike near the deadline.

label: Running the business as an unregistered partnership
best_case: Everyone pays on time and it never comes up.
worst_case: A client or a departing co-founder refuses to pay and the firm cannot sue to enforce the contract under section 69 of the Partnership Act; the founder discovers the firm has no legal standing only after paying a lawyer to find out.

sources.title: Suits by or Against Unregistered Partnership Firms: Section 69

note: Probability invented; the legal exposure itself is real and well documented.

label: Share certificates not issued within 2 months of incorporation
best_case: The CA issues them in month one along with the other paperwork, nobody notices there was ever a deadline.
worst_case: It slips past 2 months amid the general incorporation chaos. The company and the officers in default are penalised — up to ₹50,000 on the company and matching amounts split across officers — for a paperwork step nobody flagged as urgent.

sources.title: Delay in Share Certificate Issuance - Section 56(4)

note: Probability invented; deadline and penalty amounts are sourced.

label: Company goes dark instead of being formally closed
best_case: Someone remembers within a year, files the backlog, and does a fast-track strike-off for a few thousand rupees.
worst_case: Three years of missed filings later, every director is disqualified from holding directorship in any Indian company for five years, and the back-filing penalties alone cost more than the company ever earned.

sources.title: Company Strike Off Fees: STK-2 Charges Breakdown 2026

note: Trigger probability invented; the section 164(2) director-disqualification consequence is real.

label: Approved company name left unused past its reservation window
best_case: SPICe+ Part B is filed within a week of name approval, the 20-day window is never in danger.
worst_case: Something else (a co-founder disagreement, a missing document) eats the 20-60 day window. The name approval lapses, and the founder pays the ₹1,000 fee again and re-runs a process they thought was already done.

sources.title: SPICe+ Part A: Complete Guide to Company Name Reservation on MCA Portal

note: Probability invented; the 20/60-day validity rule is sourced.
